title: Adaptive Throughput Studio: UX for cache prefetch & batch tuning
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Design a compact, developer‑facing studio inside the Redwood Console that helps engineers and platform teams compose cache prefetch and batching policies. The goal is to present cost/latency tradeoffs, surface recommended safe defaults, and let users simulate workload impact before applying policies. This ticket covers interaction design, a high‑fidelity prototype, accessibility checks, and handoff artifacts for product and eng.
acceptance_criteria: Studio UI mocks (desktop) covering policy creation, quick presets, and advanced mode completed and approved by PM
Interactive Figma prototype that demonstrates: recommendations panel, explainers, guardrails slider, and workload simulator
Simulation output shows estimated tokens/sec, 95th pctl latency, and monthly cost delta for a sample workload
Design spec with component states, copy guidelines, and keyboard accessibility notes delivered to engineering
UX reviewed in design critique with documented feedback and a plan to address issues before final handoff

decisions: Expose two entry points: a compact Guided Composer for quick policy application and a full Advanced Editor for teams needing precise control
Simulations are approximate estimates (95% confidence) — product copy will call out variance and tie to a 'confidence score' returned by the backend
Guardrails default to Conservative for new accounts and Respect tenant-level overrides for Dedicated customers
Keep recommended presets as first-class UI elements with an 'explain' affordance that shows the three most important drivers for the recommendation
Shift heavy cost calculation to an async backend job; prototype will show instant client-side estimates based on sampled telemetry until the backend API is available
next_steps: Meeting with ENG on 2026-03-12 to confirm API contract for estimates (ENG-2923) and rollout plan
Product to validate guardrail wording with legal for enterprise compliance language
Design to produce a trimmed mobile layout (P2) if initial rollout shows demand from mobile console users
Prepare story map for handoff: split work into Guided Composer (MVP) and Advanced Editor (phase 2)
QA to draft test cases for simulator edge cases and accessibility checks
ux_notes: Use progressive disclosure: hide advanced knobs behind an 'Advanced' toggle to reduce cognitive load
Explanations should be short, actionable, and tied to observable metrics (cost, latency, failure rate)
Include a quick 'what-if' toggler in the simulator to run two scenarios side-by-side
Provide 'safe apply' option that creates a canary rollout with automatic rollback if latency regresses beyond threshold
